concept.name: Aroon oscillator
concept.definition: The difference between Aroon-Up and Aroon-Down, compressing Chande's pair into one line bounded between -100 and +100; positive when new highs are more recent than new lows, negative when new lows are more recent.
concept.intuition: It nets the two Aroon lines: +100 means today's bar made a new n-period high while the low is as old as possible; the zero line is the bull-bear divide.
concept.mechanics: Aroon Oscillator = Aroon-Up - Aroon-Down with the same n (default 25). Used for zero-line trend bias and, with +/-50 or +/-90 thresholds, for strong-trend filtering.
concept.formula: AroonOsc(n) = AroonUp(n) - AroonDown(n) = 100 x (PeriodsSinceLowestLow(n) - PeriodsSinceHighestHigh(n)) / n.
concept.failure_modes: It lags because it only reacts once highs and lows age out of the window; choppy markets flip it across zero repeatedly, and it was not designed for classic oscillator divergence signals.
concept.misconceptions: A positive reading does not measure trend strength in price terms - a +40 reading only ranks the recency of highs versus lows.
concept.example: Aroon-Up 80 and Aroon-Down 20 give an oscillator of +60, an upside bias; +100 requires Up = 100 and Down = 0 simultaneously.
